title: Trump's H-1B Wage Hike Could Reshape Silicon Valley Hiring
excerpt: A DOL proposed rule would lift entry-level tech salary floors to $162K in San Francisco and $113K in Dallas — reshaping how Indian-origin engineers enter the U.S. job market.
body:
The U.S. Department of Labor dropped a landmark proposed rule on March 27, 2026, that would dramatically raise the minimum wages employers must pay H-1B visa holders — and the ripple effects land squarely on the Indian tech diaspora.

**What the rule does:**
The proposal would increase Wage Level I — covering most entry-level workers — from the 17th percentile to the 34th percentile; Wage Level II from the 34th to the 52nd; Wage Level III from the 50th to the 70th; and Wage Level IV from the 67th to the 88th. In dollar terms, an entry-level software engineer in San Francisco would need to be paid at least $162,000 a year to qualify for an H-1B, the same role in Dallas would jump to about $113,000, and in New York, $132,000. The increases run nearly 30% above the current minimums in each city.

**Why it matters for Indian tech workers:**
The DOL estimates that more than 75 percent of LCA positions certified between FY 2020 and FY 2024 would fall below the proposed new wage floors. The DOL projects the rule will increase wage requirements by about $14,000 per worker, on average. This hits entry-level and early-career roles hardest — precisely the pipeline through which most Indian graduates enter the U.S. workforce after completing STEM degrees. Critics warn the rule could price smaller employers out of the H-1B system, delay green card sponsorship for junior workers, and accelerate offshoring of certain jobs.

**What to watch:**
The public comment window closes on May 26, 2026, and a final rule, in whatever form survives that process, would take effect later in 2026. The Trump administration tried to hike prevailing wages during the president's first term, leading to litigation and reversal by Biden — and legal experts say they expect litigation on the new rule as well.
